summary: The requested outcome is the mean per-object segmented cavity area fraction q, not concentration or a volume fraction. At 24 h A q=0.00446 and B q=0.08918 after similar initial means (initial_measurements.json). E02 shows different endpoint q summaries for purified length fractions but is one preparation, unequal fields, and not a calibrated mixture dose response. C01 DNA frequencies do not establish RNA production or valence; C04 phase endpoints do not map to cavity area; C03 lacks per-droplet cavity-state trajectories. The two searches produced abstract-only context: S_multiphase_wetting_domains_S3 broadly associates RNA sequence/structure/modification with RNA-condensate behavior, while S_internal_domains_rna_condensates_S2 describes coexisting nucleolar subphases and composition-linked physicochemical properties. Neither supplies the target-specific mixture-to-cavity mechanism. C05 executed successfully as an illustrative conditional calculation, not a fit. Close the literature-review task only; keep G_mix_to_internal_domain open.

candidates.target: Determine whether changing reference/variant RNA composition under controlled carryover and total RNA can trigger an internal RNA-poor domain in transcribing four-arm RNA condensates, and explain persistence.
known_relations: A/B q diverge after similar t=0 values; at 24 h A=0.00446 and B=0.08918 (initial_measurements.json).
C02 descriptive fits give model-sensitive 36/48 h extrapolations without preparation-level uncertainty.

E02 M has near-zero endpoint q while M+L and M+S are higher; one preparation, unequal fields, and no measured RNA mixing proportions.

C04 has tie-line phase concentrations and broad rectangle-propagated ratios; no phase volumes, time course, or mapping to q. Variant ratio at tie-line 0 is undefined because both concentrations are zero.
C03 does not contain longitudinal same-droplet cavity area/state or disappearance records.
S_multiphase_wetting_domains_S3 is an abstract-only RNA crowding review associating sequence, structure and modifications with condensate behavior, without a quantitative internal-domain relation.

S_internal_domains_rna_condensates_S2 is an abstract-only nucleolar study reporting coexisting subphases and composition-associated properties including pH organization; it is a biological analogue, not an engineered RNA cavity mechanism.
hypotheses: NEW, provisional and not established as novel: during transcription, a changing reference/variant RNA mixture with composition-dependent partitioning could cross a demixing threshold and nucleate an internal RNA-poor domain. Interfacial cost or slow exchange could prolong it. Retrieved sources and current measurements do not demonstrate this bridge.

gaps.description: No matched time series measures RNA proportions and phase composition alongside cavity formation/persistence in this system; wetting, interface and exchange conditions are unknown.

variables_units.q: mean per-object cavity area / filled droplet area, dimensionless [0,1]
variables_units.x: variant RNA fraction of total RNA, dimensionless [0,1], unmeasured
variables_units.xc: hypothesized threshold in x, dimensionless [0,1], unknown
variables_units.qmax: state scale for q, dimensionless [0,1], unknown
variables_units.c: hypothetical carryover driver, units depend on a direct chemical assay
variables_units.cc: hypothetical carryover threshold, same units as c

equations: Unclosed phenomenological model: dq/dt=kf*max(x-xc,0)*(qmax-q)-kc*q. It does not derive x(t), thermodynamics, or internal topology.
For fixed x and kc>0, r=kf*max(x-xc,0), q*=qmax*r/(r+kc), and q(t)=q*+(q0-q*)exp(-(r+kc)t). If x<=xc, q(t)=q0*exp(-kc*t), with half-life ln(2)/kc.
Carryover alternative: dq/dt=kg*max(c-cc,0)*(qmax-q)-kc*q. Matching kg*max(c-cc,0)=kf*max(x-xc,0) gives identical q trajectories; q(t) alone cannot identify the driver.
For species i, Ki=Ci,dense/Ci,dilute only if dilute concentration is positive; no supported mapping from Ki to image q.

parameters_ranges.kf: positive h^-1, unmeasured; C05 used illustrative 0.1-10 h^-1
parameters_ranges.kc: positive h^-1, unmeasured; C05 used illustrative 0.001-0.1 h^-1
parameters_ranges.x: [0,1]; C05 grid values are hypothetical, not observed

candidates.initial_boundary_conditions: q(0) is observed near 0.014 in A and B. x(0), phase geometry and interfaces are unknown. No spatial boundary conditions are given; this is not a spatially closed model.
candidates.observation_mapping: q maps only to the supplied per-object mean segmented empty-area fraction. It is not concentration, volume fraction, or total dark area divided by total filled area. x, c and time-varying phase concentrations are unmeasured.
alternatives: Carryover or other reaction conditions drive a global phase-state change; the same effective-rate model fits that path.
Population turnover, field sampling or segmentation changes the mean q while individual cavity states remain stable; current tracking cannot resolve that.
predictions: At matched carryover and total RNA, titrating measured RNA mixture fraction should shift q onset or steady state if composition is causal; the model predicts increasing q* above xc and relaxation toward zero below xc.

Factorially vary measured RNA composition and carryover. A composition mechanism predicts residual composition dependence at matched carryover; a pure carryover mechanism predicts response to carryover at fixed composition.
If measured x remains constant while q rises, the specific changing-composition driver is weakened. If x falls below xc, the model predicts exponential q relaxation with half-life ln(2)/kc.
checks: C05 actually executed with returncode 0 and empty stderr; it is a conditional parameter-grid calculation, not an empirical fit.
C05 matched carryover examples reproduce effective rates 0.02 h^-1 and 5 h^-1. Carryover units and values are arbitrary illustrations, not measured concentrations.
C05 code checked q* against the global maximum qmax=0.5; the closed-form expression guarantees the per-case bound q*<=the selected qmax. No temporal integration or comparison with observed q was run.

The ODE is dimensionally consistent: rates are h^-1 and q,x,xc,qmax dimensionless. For nonnegative rates q* is bounded; below threshold q decays; as kc approaches zero above threshold q* approaches qmax.

S_internal_domains_rna_condensates_S2 supplies a nucleolar multiphase analogue, not direct evidence for internal cavities in engineered RNA droplets.

final.question_and_reason: Does changing reference/variant RNA composition, with total RNA and carryover controlled, trigger an internal RNA-poor domain in transcribing four-arm RNA condensates? Current data and literature cannot distinguish that path from carryover-driven global phase change or population/measurement effects.
final.increment: S_internal_domains_rna_condensates_S2 adds a relevant but indirect precedent for coexisting subphases and composition-linked properties in an RNA-associated condensate. C05 makes the proposed ODE consequence explicit and shows why q(t) alone cannot identify composition versus carryover as the driver.
final.new_hypotheses: The system-specific mixture-threshold and persistent-internal-domain bridge is explicitly new in this investigation but novelty is unverified. It remains a hypothesis, not an explanation established by data.
final.actual_derivation_or_computation: C05 executed with returncode 0, empty stderr. It used illustrative, unfitted grids qmax={0.1,0.5}, xc={0.05,0.5}, kf={0.1,10} h^-1, kc={0.001,0.1} h^-1, x={0,0.1,0.25,0.5,1}. For fixed x, r=kf*max(x-xc,0), q*=qmax*r/(r+kc), q(t)=q*+(q0-q*)exp(-(r+kc)t). q* ranges were [0,0] at x=0, [0,0.499002] at 0.1, [0,0.499750] at 0.25, [0,0.499889] at 0.5 and [0.033333,0.499947] at 1. Matching carryover rates reproduced 0.02 and 5 h^-1 exactly within numerical precision. No fit or empirical q comparison was performed.
final.discriminating_prediction: Use matched-total-RNA composition-by-carryover factorial conditions with direct RNA composition and carryover assays. Composition causality predicts residual composition-dependent onset/steady q at matched carryover; pure carryover predicts q response to carryover at fixed composition. Measure RNA composition and phase concentrations through time and track 3D cavity state to test temporal ordering and persistence.
final.evidence_support_conflict_untested: A/B q diverges by 24 h; E02 length-fraction endpoints differ; C04 gives phase endpoints; S2 gives an abstract-only nucleolar multiphase analogue; C05 gives a conditional model consequence. E02 is not a controlled mixture titration; C04 does not map to q; DNA reads do not establish RNA abundance; tracking lacks persistent cavity state; carryover is confounded. RNA composition over time, cavity identity/geometry, wetting and exchange remain untested.
final.decision: Complete the literature-review task; keep the mechanistic gap open. The conditional mixture-threshold model is not a validated explanation.
final.dissent: R2 did not have S_internal_domains_rna_condensates_S2 and therefore could not assess that analogy. R3 correctly treats it as relevant multiphase context while leaving the causal gap open. C05 is illustrative and non-identifying; the global bound check was corrected by the analytic per-case bound.
final.next_experiment: Matched-total-RNA factorial composition and carryover perturbation, with direct RNA-species/carryover measurements, serial phase-composition measurements, and longitudinal 3D cavity tracking. No physical experiment occurred in this run.
final.limitations: All literature support is abstract-only. C05 parameters are illustrative and unfitted; the ODE omits spatial geometry and thermodynamics. q is segmented area, not concentration or phase volume. Preparation-level replication is limited; no causal intervention was conducted.
